description: Renders slides you wrote as HTML on a slide deck's template, so you can design slides yourself instead of asking the slides agent. It saves nothing. Each draft answers its image, the issues to fix and notes to check by eye: fix the issues and render again until none are left. Call getReportDesign first and follow the guide it answers. A chart or table a draft places is drawn with its datasheet's data, or with the data of datasheetChanges you tried with previewReportDatasheetChanges and have not saved yet: save them with saveReportDatasheetChanges before you save the slides. Only the report's editors may. At most 10 drafts a call, and 20 renders and saves a minute per user.

__schema0.description: The report to act on, by its `id` from `listReports` or `createReport`. Only reports whose `type` is `SlideDeck` work here: another type, such as a Google Slides presentation, returns `400`. You can also copy it from the report's link in Rollstack: it's the part right after `/slides/`.

__schema1.description: The draft slides to render, 1 to 10 a call, each under an id of its own.

name.description: The column that holds each row's label, such as "Year"

rows.description: One output row per input row and entry, in this order; the input columns no entry names repeat on each

values.description: The columns the values go in: one, such as "Value", or one per measure

columns.description: The input column for each of values, in order; null leaves that value empty on this row

label.description: What the name column says on this row, such as the column's name or "2022"

__schema13.description: Columns worked out on each source row before the filters and the grouping, which filters, dimensions, splits and measures can then name like a source column. A formula reads one row only and may name an earlier custom field. Examples: price times quantity, summed by region; deal-size bands with if(); diff_days between two dates, then averaged

formula.description: A formula over one source row: ${Column} names a source column or an earlier custom field. No sum(), mean(), min(), max(), median(), count(), offset(), index() or running_total(), which read other rows

__schema16.description: A formula: ${Column} names a dimension or measure by its name before renames; numbers, "text", yes, no, null; + - * / (dividing by 0 gives empty); = != < <= > >=; AND, OR, NOT; if(condition, then, else), coalesce(a, b), round(x, digits), abs(x), concat(a, b), is_null(x), to_string(x); sum(x), mean(x), min(x) and max(x) of a column over the rows shown, after the row limit, such as ${Sales} / sum(${Sales}) for each row's share of the rows shown; offset(x, n), the value n rows below in the rows shown (-1 the row above, empty past the first or last), and index(x, n), the value in row n of the rows shown (counting from 1), such as ${Sales} - offset(${Sales}, 1) for the lead over the next row; median(x), and count(x) of its values that aren't empty, over the rows shown; running_total(x), the sum of x from the first row shown down to this one, in the rows' order; power(x, y), x to the power y (empty for a negative x with a fractional y); diff_days(start, end), the whole days from the start date to the end date, negative when the end is earlier, empty when either is empty

__schema17.description: A column name, exact and case-sensitive

bucket.description: A date unit to group a date or timestamp column by (month: each month of each year), a part of the date over every year (month_of_year: Jan to Dec, quarter_of_year: 1 to 4, day_of_week: Mon to Sun), else null. This year beside last year by month is month_of_year split by the year

fill.description: A date grouped by a unit or a part only, one key at most: every period between the first and the last (every month, quarter or weekday of a part), for each combination of the other keys, a count or sum of no rows as 0. Omit to show only the periods the rows have

groups.description: A text column only: values shown under one name, e.g. Email and Telephone as "Email & Tel"; the others keep theirs

html.description: The slide as one `<section>` of HTML, as large as the report's canvas. No scripts, embedded pages, event attributes or anything loaded from outside it.

id.description: The id you give the slide: letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64 characters. Pass an existing slide's id to redraw that slide.

as.description: Omit for the default name, such as "Sum of Sales"

column.description: null only with count, which counts rows

filters.description: Only the rows these all match, beside measures of every row: e.g. a count of the mortgages that are Buy to Let. Omit for every row

__schema3.description: Changes to the report's datasheets that aren't saved yet, the ones you tried with `previewReportDatasheetChanges`: the drafts draw their charts and tables with the data they give, and a new datasheet is placed by the id the preview answered. Save them with `saveReportDatasheetChanges` before you save the slides.

__schema4.description: The changes to the report's datasheets, applied in order: `create` for a datasheet the report doesn't have yet (a query, one SQL statement, or a join and steps over elements that datasheets of the report read already, under a `temporaryId` you choose), `set-query` or `set-ops` for the data of one it has (`getReportDatasheet` gives what it is now), `set-read-type` and `set-unpivot`. Each datasheet is its reads followed by the ops over them: call `getReportDataGuide` for the query model, SQL and joins. A `temporaryId` can be used once: after a save, create the next datasheet under another.

__schema40.description: last/next only: whole units, leaving out the current one, e.g. the last 3 complete months on Oct 21 are Jul, Aug and Sep. Omit for the window through today

__schema42.description: With complete only: the current unit too, e.g. the last 1 complete year with the current one is last year and this year. Omit to leave it out

__schema44.description: current only: the unit so far, through today, e.g. this year to date. Omit for the whole unit

__schema46.description: current/last only: the same window, this many units earlier: this year to date 1 year earlier is the same dates last year, and the last 3 complete months 3 months earlier are the 3 months before them. Omit for the window itself

__schema48.description: Dimensions whose values become columns, outer first: each level splits the one above; empty for none

__schema49.description: Columns beside each row over every row the aggregate gives: a rank, a percent of total, a difference or percent difference from the previous row ordered by the only dimension, a total/average/min/max of a measure, or a formula over the row's dimensions and measures, such as a rate. A formula with sum(), mean(), min() or max() reads only the rows the limit keeps, such as each top 10 row's share of the 10. Need a dimension or measure and no split

formats.description: With ops; a query has its own formats

ops.description: Only over several reads: a join step over every read first, naming each read in its inputs (from op, ref the read alias), then steps

parameters.description: User-controlled periods, limits, thresholds and selections: SQL reads them as columns of the params input, a step as {"type":"parameter","key":"<key>"}

query.description: The data as the Edit data editor builds it, over the one read; give query, or ops over several reads

reads.description: The elements it reads, each once: the one a query reads, or those a join reads

sql.description: In place of a query or ops: one DuckDB SELECT over the reads, each a table named by its alias, with its formats in formats. Only for what a query can't do, such as a date stored as text (`CAST("Month" AS DATE) AS "Month"`) or a figure from two datasheets that read one row each (`SELECT won."Revenue" / goal."Goal" AS "Share of goal" FROM won, goal`)

temporaryId.description: A stable id for the new datasheet, which later changes in this patch reference it by

query.description: The data as the Edit data editor builds it, replacing all the datasheet's ops but its read: getReportDatasheet gives its current query to start from

formats.description: Replaces the datasheet's formats; omit to keep them

ops.description: The complete op list after the reads, in run order: an op whose ref is an existing op id keeps that op, and existing ops left out are removed. Only on a datasheet with a join step: keep the join first with steps after it; on any other, use set-query

readType.description: aggregated: its data, as the tool displays it; raw: its tidy read, to transform; image: its picture

unpivot.description: The columns of the range this datasheet reads to turn into rows, which every datasheet reading the range raw gets, and this one then reads it raw; null reads the range as the sheet shows it

offset.description: How many rows back to compare with; omit for 1, the previous row

orderBy.description: The query's only dimension, such as a month, by its name before renames: the rows are ordered by it, oldest first

__schema52.description: A measure, by its name before renames

__schema53.description: The new column's name. Omit for the default name

__schema55.description: Every column once, by its name before renames, in the order to show them, removed columns optional; omit for dimensions, measures, then calculations

__schema57.description: Omit for the default: columns in the order their values first appear

values.description: One column per value, each under its own name: two values never share a column

fill.description: Value for empty cells; null leaves them empty

nullLabel.description: Column name for NULL values; null drops them

alias.description: The name SQL reads this element by in FROM/JOIN, and ops name it by as a ref

datasheetRef.description: An existing datasheet that reads one element: the new datasheet reads that element, with its filters

readType.description: Omit to read it as that datasheet does

__schema66.description: Columns to sort by, the first first, each next one breaking ties; empty for none

column.description: A column, by its name before renames; a split's cell by its values

__schema68.description: Rows to keep: a number, an integer parameter, or null for all

__schema71.description: A table's total row and, with a split, its Total column, each measure over the rows shown (under a limit, only those). Omit for none

column.description: With a pivot after the aggregate: a Total column with each row across the pivot

row.description: A last row with the total of each column; charts leave it out

column.description: An output column, by the name it is shown under, after any rename

__schema76.description: Columns, by their name before renames, to leave out of the rows while keeping the grouping, e.g. group by region and month but show no region column; a split's column is named by its values

__schema78.description: Conditions on the grouped rows' dimensions and measures (by their name before renames), all of which must hold, right after the grouping and before the calculations, the sort and the limit, as SQL's HAVING does, so the calculations and the limit only see the rows kept: each region's share among the regions with more than 20 deals. To keep rows by a measure or a calculation while the calculations still cover every group, as for the top 10 of the customers over 1,000,000, use keepRowsBeforeLimit. Needs a dimension or measure and no split

__schema80.description: Conditions on the grouped rows' dimensions, measures and before-limit calculations (by their name before renames), all of which must hold, after the calculations and before the column order, the sort and the limit, so the limit counts only the rows kept while the calculations still cover every group: the top 10 customers of those over 1,000,000, the regions with over 5% of the total. A condition on a calculation that reads the rows the limit keeps (sum(), offset()) goes in keepRowsWhere. Needs a dimension or measure and no split

__schema82.description: Conditions on the rows' own columns (dimensions, measures and calculations by their name before renames), all of which must hold, after the sort, the limit and every calculation: keep the rank 1 row of the top 10, with its share of the 10. To keep rows before the limit, use keepRowsBeforeLimit. Needs a dimension or measure and no split

inputs.description: Omit to keep a kept op wired as it is (one that read the op above reads its new op above). A new op reads the op above, which SQL reads as `input`; a new first op reads the datasheet's one read, as `source` or the read's alias

ref.description: An existing op id to keep that op, or a new short name

step.description: A step op's call; on a kept op, send it only to change it

title.description: Omit to keep a kept op's title; a step op without one shows its step summary

alias.description: SQL ops: the name the statement reads this input by

from.description: previous: the op above (above the first op, the datasheet's one read); op: the one ref names

ref.description: op: the ref of an earlier op in this list, or a read's operation id or alias

params.description: The params of its fn, whose exact JSON Schema getReportDataGuide answers when you name the fn in stepFunctions

__schema94.description: numfmt formats by output column: give each renamed or computed number or date column one

__schema96.description: An existing datasheet id, or the temporaryId of a datasheet created earlier in this patch

__schema97.description: Replaces the datasheet's complete parameter set; omit to keep it

body.description: What the tool creates, changes or sends

params.description: The ids of what the tool acts on
